name: Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for MPNST

criteria.description: Presence of spindle-shaped tumor cells with nuclear atypia and high mitotic activity on histopathology
Loss or reduced expression of S-100 protein and positive staining for SOX10 or other Schwann cell markers
Association with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) or arising from a pre-existing benign nerve sheath tumor
MRI showing a large, heterogeneous mass with necrosis and peripheral enhancement along a peripheral nerve distribution

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with characteristic spindle cell morphology and immunohistochemical profile consistent with MPNST
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, radiological, and pathological findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rapidly enlarging painful peripheral nerve mass
Neuropathic motor weakness in affected nerve distribution

common.symptomName: Paresthesia or numbness in affected limb
searchTerms: loss of sensation in arm or leg

common.symptomName: Pain exacerbated by nerve compression or movement
Muscle atrophy distal to tumor site
searchTerms: loss of muscle bulk in limb

occasional.symptomName: Cutaneous hyperpigmentation or café-au-lait spots (in NF1-associated cases)
Constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever or weight loss
searchTerms: general symptoms like fatigue and low fever
loss of feeling outside nerve path

occasional.symptomName: Joint stiffness or decreased range of motion near tumor site
searchTerms: difficulty bending joint close to mass

rare.symptomName: Pathological fracture due to bone invasion
searchTerms: fractures caused by cancer in bone

rare.notes: Note: lymphatic system is not in valid body systems; consider immunological

rare.symptomName: Respiratory distress from thoracic tumor extension
searchTerms: respiratory distress due to tumor growth

laboratory: Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in some cases
No specific blood markers diagnostic for MPNST
imaging: MRI showing heterogeneous mass with areas of necrosis and peripheral enhancement
genetic: Loss of NF1 gene function in NF1-associated cases
Complex karyotypic abnormalities including TP53 mutations
other: Histopathology revealing spindle cells with high mitotic index and necrosis
Immunohistochemistry positive for SOX10, variable S-100 protein expression

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of significant nuclear atypia and mitotic activity
Slow growth and absence of pain
Typically arises near joints rather than along nerves

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of a previously stable nerve sheath tumor
New onset of severe neuropathic pain or motor weakness
Presence of necrosis or heterogeneous enhancement on imaging
references: Stucky CC et al. Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumors: Clinicopathologic Study of 120 Cases. Cancer. 2012.
Evans DG et al. Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumours in neurofibromatosis 1. J Med Genet. 2002.
WHO Classification of Tumours Editorial Board. Soft Tissue and Bone Tumours. 5th Edition. 2020.
